result.title: ReCoCo: From Patches to Compositions for Visual Representation Learning
result.summary: Self-supervised learning has produced powerful visual representations, yet learning strong dense features remains challenging. While consistency between augmented views provides strong image-level supervision, extending this principle to local visual content is less straightforward. Existing approaches often match individual patches across views or identify coherent regions, introducing uncertainties in correspondence estimation and assumptions about how visual content should be grouped. We introduce ReCoCo (Regional Composition Consistency), a principled approach that extends cross-view consistency to the regional level without requiring such correspondences or semantic grouping. ReCoCo represents the content shared between augmented views through compositions of their patch-level predictions over learned visual prototypes. By aligning these compositions, the model learns from regions containing multiple visual concepts without requiring them to be separated beforehand. ReCoCo integrates naturally with teacher-student self-distillation and introduces no additional learned parameters. Extensive experiments demonstrate substantial improvements in frozen-feature segmentation, clustering, and regional retrieval while maintaining competitive image-level recognition, alleviating the trade-off between dense and global representation quality.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ReCoCo，将跨视图一致性从 patch 级提升到区域级：用 patch 预测在学习到的视觉原型上的组合来表示两视图共享内容并加以对齐，无需显式对应估计或语义分组，直接嵌入 teacher-student 自蒸馏框架且不增加参数，在冻结特征的分割、聚类与区域检索上取得提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「以原型分布组合替代逐点对应」的免对应区域级自蒸馏监督，可供核查是否能用于训练 VLM 内部视觉状态，使 latent 表征在位置偏移与多概念混合下仍保留区域证据，但该文不涉及推理期状态生成或答案使用，联系仅为训练监督线索。
